strengths: Novel and well-motivated task formulation: The paper formalizes text-driven amodal 3D generation, addressing a fundamental limitation of current feedforward image-to-3D models that collapse to observation-overfitted modes under severe occlusion.

Clever training-free design: RelaxFlow cleverly decouples observation fidelity from semantic disambiguation via dual-branch ODE interpolation, visual multi-prior consensus, attention-logit smoothing (low-pass relaxation), and visibility-aware velocity blending without requiring expensive model retraining.

Theoretical grounding: The manuscript provides a solid theoretical analysis connecting attention-logit smoothing to low-pass filtering on the generative vector field, showing that suppressing high-frequency noise leads to tighter Wasserstein bounds and more stable trajectories.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Evaluated across two representative feedforward 3D backbones (SAM3D and TRELLIS) on two diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D), RelaxFlow shows consistent improvements in both quantitative metrics (Point-FID, CLIP scores, LPIPS) and user preferences.
weaknesses: Reliance on 2D visual proxies: Because current feedforward 3D models are vision-conditioned, RelaxFlow relies on retrieving or synthesizing 2D prior images using an external model (e.g., Z-Image) rather than direct text conditioning. While practical, the final 3D quality and semantic consistency remain contingent on the fidelity and diversity of these visual proxies.

Modest benchmark scale for semantic branching: The AmbiSem-3D benchmark contains only 21 curated test cases. While valuable as a diagnostic benchmark with human evaluation, evaluating on a broader and more diverse set would provide stronger statistical confidence.

Idealized theoretical assumptions: The theoretical proofs rely on strong assumptions (e.g., Assumptions A.2 and A.3 regarding the strict low-pass nature of the semantic transport field and high-frequency nature of estimation errors, as well as global Lipschitz continuity across cross-attention layers), which are idealized approximations of complex non-linear generative networks.

strengths: Relevant and well-motivated problem formulation: Formalizing text-driven amodal 3D generation tackles a clear failure mode of feedforward 3D foundation models (e.g., SAM3D, TRELLIS), which often collapse to a single hallucinated mode or overfit visible geometry when occlusions are severe.

Training-free and modular design: RelaxFlow operates purely at inference time via dual-branch ODE velocity blending, multi-prior cross-attention consensus, and visibility-aware masking, requiring no costly retraining or fine-tuning of 3D generator backbones.

Interesting theoretical framing: Modeling the dual-branch guidance as an ODE interpolation and attempting to formalize structural guidance via low-pass filtering and Lipschitz/Wasserstein stability bounds provides valuable conceptual motivation.

Dedicated diagnostic benchmarks: The curation of ExtremeOcc-3D (264 cases with >=80% natural occlusion) and AmbiSem-3D (semantic branching scenarios) provides a useful testbed for amodal completion under underdetermined conditions.

Thorough empirical analysis and transparent limitations: The manuscript includes comprehensive component ablations (Table 5a, Figure 5b), user studies, and explicitly discusses failure cases (e.g., concept fusion under incompatible observations and priors in Appendix G).
weaknesses: Theoretical gap between token logit smoothing and spatial velocity filtering: The theoretical proofs in Appendix A assume Gaussian smoothing directly on the vector field in state/spatial frequency domain, whereas the actual implementation applies 1D/2D Gaussian blur over the cross-attention logit matrix across discrete token sequences. Because the mapping from attention logits through softmax, projections, and deep transformer blocks to continuous velocity fields is highly non-linear, the theoretical claim that attention logit smoothing is equivalent to low-pass filtering the velocity field remains an unproven heuristic approximation.

Heavy reliance on 2D image proxies / external T2I models: Because existing 3D models operate in visual-token spaces, the method requires retrieving or synthesizing N prior images using an external model (e.g., Z-Image). Consequently, prompt fidelity is fundamentally bottlenecked by the quality, viewpoint, and biases of the 2D proxy generator.

Limited scale of AmbiSem-3D: The AmbiSem-3D benchmark consists of only 21 curated test cases, which is relatively small for drawing statistically conclusive evaluation, even if supplemented with user studies.

Sensitivity to blending and scheduling hyperparameters: The pipeline introduces several hand-crafted heuristic schedules and parameters (cutoff threshold rho, smoothing width sigma, z-buffer dilation k, and soft-visibility decay factors lambda, beta, gamma). As shown in Figure 5a, performance degrades substantially when rho or sigma deviate from default values, indicating potential sensitivity across different domains or camera configurations.

strengths: Compelling and well-motivated problem formulation: Formalizing text-driven amodal 3D generation addresses a realistic failure mode of modern feedforward 3D generators, which collapse into arbitrary or observation-overfitted modes under extreme occlusion.

Clever, training-free design: RelaxFlow operates purely at inference time as a plug-and-play module over state-of-the-art flow backbones (e.g., TRELLIS and SAM3D) without requiring expensive retraining or fine-tuning on occluded 3D data.

Principled decoupling of control granularities: The dual-branch ODE formulation—combining rigid feature anchoring for visible evidence with low-pass smoothed attention logits for the semantic prior—is conceptually elegant and supported by a spectral/Wasserstein stability derivation.
Creation of two diagnostic benchmarks: ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D fill an important gap in evaluating semantic disambiguation and amodal fidelity under occlusion and multi-hypothesis ambiguity.

Convincing empirical validation: Substantial quantitative gains across metrics (e.g., Point-FID, FID, CLIP text-image alignment), comprehensive ablations on key components (visibility mask, smoothing kernel, cutoff schedule), and an informative user study.
weaknesses: Reliance on visual proxy generation/retrieval: Because existing 3D backbones accept visual tokens rather than text tokens directly, the pipeline relies on an auxiliary 2D T2I generator (Z-Image) or image retrieval. Any domain gap or artifacts in the generated 2D priors could impact downstream guidance.

Scale of AmbiSem-3D benchmark: While the benchmark is carefully curated across three ambiguity categories, 21 cases is relatively small; expanding this set would offer even stronger statistical validation.

Sensitivity to geometric visibility estimation: The fine-grained SLAT velocity blending relies on z-buffer reprojection and estimated camera poses. When pose estimation is unavailable (as noted for TRELLIS), the geometric visibility mask must be disabled, leading to reduced performance.

Idealized theoretical assumptions: The theoretical proof rests on assumptions that semantic transport fields are strictly band-limited to low frequencies and network prediction errors reside purely in high frequencies, which are strong idealizations of complex multimodal generative vector fields.

strengths: Compelling problem formulation: Formalizes text-driven amodal 3D generation to resolve occlusion ambiguity, moving beyond conventional single-mode feedforward hallucination toward explicit, controllable 3D completion.

Clever, training-free design: The dual-branch ODE interpolation framework elegantly decouples rigid observation constraints from relaxed structural priors. Leveraging attention-logit smoothing to extract coarse structural guidance from visual proxies without retraining is practical and effective.

Theoretical justification: Provides a well-formulated theoretical analysis showing that logit smoothing acts as a low-pass filter on the generative velocity field, accompanied by stability and Wasserstein-2 error bounds under Lipschitz assumptions.

Thorough evaluation and diagnostic benchmarks: Introduces two specialized benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D), extensively tests against multiple baseline paradigms (2D editing, video generation, multi-view diffusion, feedforward amodal models), and includes a user study and informative ablations.
weaknesses: Inference latency: Evaluating dual flow branches increases wall-clock inference time significantly (e.g., a 2.46× overhead on SAM3D, from ~15.6s to ~38.4s per sample).

Reliance on visual proxy generators: Converting text intent into 2D proxy images via text-to-image generation (or retrieval) introduces external dependencies; failure modes or style biases in the proxy generator could affect 3D semantic steering.

Theoretical assumptions: The assumption that true semantic guidance is strictly low-frequency while velocity errors are strictly high-frequency is an idealized spectral model that is conceptually intuitive but difficult to verify empirically in deep neural feature spaces.

strengths: Well-motivated task formulation: The paper formalizes 'text-driven amodal 3D generation', which addresses a genuine limitation of current feedforward single-image 3D generators—namely, their tendency to collapse to a single, dataset-biased hallucination when encountering severe occlusion or ambiguous view angles.

Practical training-free design: RelaxFlow operates at inference time on top of existing rectified-flow 3D backbones (e.g., SAM3D, TRELLIS) without requiring costly retraining or per-scene optimization.

Decoupled control granularity: The combination of a strict observation branch, an attention-smoothed semantic-prior branch, multi-prior consensus tokens, and visibility-aware depth masking provides an effective and modular design for balancing evidence preservation with semantic steering.

Thorough comparative evaluation: The authors benchmark against a diverse set of pipelines including feedforward occlusion-aware models (SAM3D, Amodal3R), multi-view methods (MV-Adapter), video-to-3D pipelines (Wan2.2-TI2V), and 2D-editing-then-lifting approaches, supported by both automatic metrics and a user study.
weaknesses: Theoretical gap between logit smoothing and velocity-field filtering: The manuscript claims that the relaxation mechanism is 'proven to be equivalent to applying a low-pass filter on the generative vector field'. In reality, smoothing the pre-softmax attention logits across spatial token dimensions within intermediate transformer layers does not strictly convolve the downstream vector field with a Gaussian filter; rather, the authors establish an upper bound via Lipschitz smoothness (Assumption A.11). Claiming strict equivalence is an overstatement.

Heuristic spectral assumptions: Proposition A.4 and the stability analysis rely heavily on Assumptions A.2 and A.3 (that semantic velocity is band-limited while semantic estimation error is strictly high-frequency). In practice, semantic mismatch can introduce low-frequency global structural distortions (e.g., generating completely wrong limbs or gross geometric deformation), which cannot simply be eliminated by a Gaussian blur.

Limited size of the primary branching benchmark: The curated diagnostic benchmark AmbiSem-3D consists of only 21 cases in the main benchmark. While the appendix includes a 100-case extension (AmbiSem-3D-Ext), 21 test samples is very small for establishing statistically reliable automatic metric conclusions.

Heavy reliance on external text-to-image proxies and retrieval: Because feedforward 3D backbones expect visual conditioning tokens, the semantic guidance hinges on generating high-quality reference images via off-the-shelf 2D diffusion models (e.g., Z-Image). Any artifacts, background clutter, or non-canonical poses in these 2D proxies risk polluting the 3D generation.

Computational latency overhead: Maintaining dual forward trajectories (evaluating both observation and prior velocity fields during early denoising steps) alongside processing concatenated token sequences from N=3 prior images results in a ~1.8x to ~2.5x increase in inference wall-clock time compared to standard feedforward backbones.

strengths: Novel and practically relevant task formulation: The paper formalizes text-driven amodal 3D generation to resolve occlusion ambiguity, moving beyond single-mode collapse in standard feedforward image-to-3D models.

Principled and training-free design: RelaxFlow introduces an elegant dual-branch ODE formulation that decouples rigid observation adherence from relaxed structural guidance via attention logit smoothing and visibility-aware spatial-temporal blending without requiring model retraining.

Solid theoretical underpinning: The authors establish a rigorous connection between cross-attention logit smoothing and low-pass filtering of the generative vector field, providing proofs for error reduction and Wasserstein-2 stability bounds under Lipschitz continuity.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The paper constructs two diagnostic benchmarks (ExtremeOcc-3D and AmbiSem-3D), conducts extensive comparisons across multiple baseline families (2D editing, video-to-3D, multi-view diffusion), provides detailed ablations, and validates qualitative superiority through a 32-participant user study.
weaknesses: Dependence on external 2D prior generation: While framed as 'text-driven', the method relies on generating or retrieving multiple clean visual proxies (e.g., using Z-Image with specific prompt engineering) to interface with visual-token conditioned backbones, adding pipeline complexity.
Inference computational overhead: Evaluating dual branches and modifying attention increases wall-clock inference runtime considerably (e.g., 2.46x overhead on SAM3D, taking ~38s vs 15.6s per asset).

Small diagnostic benchmark size: The primary AmbiSem-3D dataset comprises only 21 curated instances; although an extended 100-case set is provided in the appendix, broader large-scale validation across diverse open-world categories remains somewhat limited.

Idealized spectral assumptions: The theoretical proofs rely on strong assumptions (Assumptions A.2 and A.3) that semantic transport is strictly low-frequency and neural velocity estimation errors are strictly high-frequency, which are conceptual approximations of complex transformer behavior.
